newsitem.title: UK: From the Flightdeck - The Air Cargo Week In Review.
newsitem.headline: From the Flightdeck - The Air Cargo Week In Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' look back at the major developments in the air cargo industry in the week October 11 - October 18.
**OCTOBER 11*
FRANKFURT - Lufthansa says it will add three new Swedish destinations in co-operation with code-share partner SAS from October 27.
SINGAPORE - ANA official says it is to increase it international passenger revenue by eight percent annually.
STOCKHOLM - Air France says it would consider stepping up the frequency of its weekly Paris-Helsinki-Stockholm-Paris freighter operation.
PARIS - Korean Airlines Paris cargo manager says it had replaced a Boeing 747-200 freighter with a 747-400 on a scheduled service between Paris and Seoul, effective last month.
STOCKHOLM - Sweden's civil aviation authority figures showed Stockholm's international Arlanda airport handled 104,312 tonnes of cargo in 1995, 12 percent more than in the previous year.
PARIS - Airport authority figures show airfreight traffic handled at Lyon-Satolas airport in the first nine months of the year totalled 15,475 tonnes, up 8.7 percent on the same period in 1995.
LONDON - MSAS Cargo says it will open in October a new office and warehouse facility in the Pudong Free Trade Zone, east of Shanghai.
LONDON - DHL managing director Nick Butcher says the future for freight forwarders "is rather modest compared to an exciting one foretold for express carriers".

PARIS - Korean Airlines assistant cargo manager, Europe says its individual cargo stations in continental Europe will have a free hand in implementing measures they deemed appropriate to improve yields.
SINGAPORE - ANA managing director of sales and marketing says it is interested in establishing air links from Kansai to U.S. cities like Honolulu, Los Angeles and New York.
LONDON - The Times newspaper reports the UK government is set to approve the proposed alliance between BA and American Airlines.

MILAN - An Italian newspaper reported Alitalia is close to reached a deal to sublease five Fokker airliners and hand over several of its national and international routes to private carrier Alpi Eagles.
**OCTOBER 14**
PARIS - Les Echos financial newspaper says Air France and Continental Airlines are in advanced stages of discussions towards signing an alliance deal.
BARCELONA - The airport authority says cargo traffic at Spain's Barcelona airport increased 8.58 percent in September compared with the same month last year to 6,355 tonnes.
VITORIA - The airport authority says cargo traffic at Vitoria airport in northern Spain rose 97 percent in September to 2,184 tonnes from 1,110 tonnes in September 1995.
REDWOOD CITY - DHL Airways says it has promoted Victor Guinasso, who has been with the company for 14 years, to president of the international air express network's U.S. operations.
LONDON - Analysts says shares in BA rose in early trade on Monday, helped by the report the British government is poised to approve BA's proposed alliance with American Airlines.
STOCKHOLM - Sweden's civil aviation authority says Stockholm's international airport loaded and unloaded 25,831 tonnes of mail in 1995, a rise of 8.6 percent over the previous year.
MOSCOW - Russian carrier Transearo says that it would begin regular flights this month from Moscow to Akmola, the planned new capital of Kazakhstan, and to the central Russian city of Samara.
LONDON - MSAS says it is the first management company to sign a letter of intent for space at Hong Kong's new airport Chek Lap Kok.
STOCKHOLM - Finland's aviation authority says Finnish airport handled 10.2 percent more cargo and 8.2 percent more mail in September this year compared to a year ago.
NEW YORK - The Wall Street Journal says USAir Group is thinking about ordering upto 120 new jetliners in a deal worth more than $5 billion.
MOSCOW - Russia's Aeroflot spokeswoman says it will launch a regular service between Moscow and Mauritius from November 1.
PARIS - Airport authority figures show Lille-Lesquin airport, in northern France, handled 2,212 tonnes of cargo traffic last month, up 13 percent on September 1995.
BRUSSELS - Airport figures show Ostend handled 5,741 tonnes of air cargo traffic last month, an increase of 7.1 percent on September 1995.
HONG KONG - U-Freight managing director Anthony Fong says it is considering opening an office in Guangzhou to take advantage of China Southern Airlines' growing international network.
AMMAN - Jordan state-airline Royal Jordania planning department says it saw a 6.2 percent rise in passenger traffic in the first nine months of 1996, compared to the same period last year.
VIENNA - Lauda Air says it expected 1995/96 full-year earnings to be on par with last year's results.
BRUSSELS - The EC says it was reviewing the proposed takeover of TNT by Dutch PTT Post BV.
LONDON - National Express Group says passenger traffic at the East Midlands airport fell 8.1 percent in the third quarter from a year ago to 640,000.
* Birmingham International airport says that it handled 588,655 passengers in September, 1.3 percent than a year ago.
BUDAPEST - Airline and airport officials says Budapest's Ferihegy airport reduced delays over customs clearance of imported cargo to two days from three-four days.
PARIS - The president of the Creteil commercial court says a decision on the fate of Air Liberte is not due before next week and no bidder has yet formally submitted an offer.
PARIS - French electronics firm Thomson-CSF says its Airsys subsidiary won a contract to supply navigation and landing aids for Sarajevo airport.
PARIS - Airbus Industrie says it was in negotiations with USAir Group to sell it passenger jets.
KANSAS CITY - Vanguard Airlines says it expects to show a loss for the third quarter ended September 30, 1996.
MADRID - A cargo official says Iberia is planning to schedule a second-weekly 747 freighter from Barcelona and Madrid to Buenos Aires, possibly starting on October 17.
LONDON - BA says it has bid 3.0 million stg to acquire the assets of troubled French regional airline Air Liberte.
FRANKFURT - A Reuters' market survey shows air cargo market rates in Germany have picked up in reaction to an autumn upturn in demand and a Lufthansa rates increase.
ROME - Air Madagascar sales director says it plans to restart a weekly Rome service, after a nine year break, using a 747-200 from December 18.
AMSTERDAM - Korean Air cargo manager Mike Zimmerman says it is delaying the introduction of a second freighter into Schiphol airport.
AALSMEER - The Dutch flower export council says the total value of Dutch exports of flowers and plants grew 7.9 percent in September to 564 million guilders.
PARIS - CDR Enterprises, parent company of AOM says it does not plan to bid for Air Liberte.
INDIANAPOLIS - American Trans Air Inc. says its September passenger load factor declined four points to 64.0 points from 68.0 percent a YEAR AGO.
ST LOUIS - TWA says it matched discounts of up to 50 percent made by Continental Airlines on domestic flights and flights to Toronto and San Juan.

MIAMI - An attorney in the case says a new trial date of November 12 has been set in the lawsuit that five airlines filed against Florida's Dade County over the bond financing formula for a new American Airlines terminal at Miami International airport.
RICHMOND - State officials says Virginia department of Aviation will conduct a study of airport needs in central and eastern Virginia, identifying possibly sites for a major regional airport.
SEATTLE - Boeing Co. says that it is bidding for a potentially major order for new jets from USAir Group.
CASABLANCA - A spokesman says Morocco's state airline Royal Air Maroc announced it had launched a bid with a French group to purchase the insolvent Air Liberte.
**OCTOBER 15**
PARIS - French newspapers say Virgin Express and a consortium led by French travel company Nouvelles Frontieres have bid for Air Liberte.
AMSTERDAM - Polar Air Inter aviation services director says it is increasing its weekly Amsterdam freight flights to New York to three with effect from October 15.
SINGAPORE - Aviation analysts says strong passenger traffic growth should partly offset higher jet fuel prices for Singapore Airlines, which is due to release its first half results on October 27.
BANGKOK - A senior official says the Thai Cabinet approved a proposal to allow Thai Airways International to hold a stake in a new cargo company.
HONG KONG - Investment banks Salomon Brothers forecast "phenomenal" long term growth prospects for Thai Airways and says management is "finally getting serious" about cargo.
* Hong Kong Air Cargo Terminals says it is on course for another record year with a 7.1 percent increase in throughout during September.
FRANKFURT - Air cargo communications system Traxon says it recorded 31.8 percent growth in transmissions in Europe over the first eight months of 1996.
LISBON - A spokesman says the Portuguese government will delay until the end of next week the announcement of the winner of a competition to provide a new medium haul fleet for state-airline TAP.
FRANKFURT - An industry survey shows Germany shippers and forwarders see Lufthansa Cargo as the closest to an ideal cargo airline.

RIO DE JANEIRO - A newspaper says Brazil national airline Varig is due to unveil a new image and expansion plans in an effort to return to profitability after first half losses of around $150 million.
FRANKFURT - Thai Airways says its new Frankfurt-Asia freighter service has generated high load factors on its first two flights.

MOSCOW - A senior aviation official says cash-strapped Russian airlines bought only four Russian-made aircraft between January and September of this year compared with 22 planes in the same period of 1995.

TORONTO - Air Canada and Lufthansa says they are to launch the second phase of their extensive international marketing alliance: the start of twice-daily, non-stop flights from both Toronto and Frankfurt, effective October 27.
INDIANAPOLIS - Amtran Inc says Dan Quayle, former vice-president of the U.S., resigned from its board of directors.
ARLINGTON - USAir says that it has served papers to BA and American Airlines that provide legal and factual details supporting its suit against them.
LONDON - Forum co-ordinator Martin Richards says the first meeting of the UK Air Freight forum will take place on November 5, and include airlines, freight forwarders and shipper representatives.

DARIEN, Connecticut - AEI and IBM Group says they have agreed to a three-year contract covering air freight and customs brokerage service which AEI is to provide across part of the computer group's global network.

PARIS - Jacques Maillot, chairman of travel group Nouvelles Frontieres and airline Corsair says a consortium he was heading "had the capital it needs" for succeeding in obtaining control over ailing airline Air Liberte.
LONDON - Virgin Group spokesman says Virgin Express has been in direct contact with a court-appointed liquidator in connection with troubled Air Liberte.
LUXEMBOURG - A senior EC source says the EU agreed to liberalise ground-handling services at airports in the 15-country bloc, confirming a decision transport ministers made last December.
PARIS - Air France says its September global cargo traffic at 434.9 million FTK's was 12.9 percent above September 1995.
* French aviation executives says they feared renewed turbulence with the U.S. over airline market access in France, with Air France caught up in a looming "air war".
MONTREAL - Air Canada says it flew 5.5 percent more revenue passenger miles in September 1996 than in the same month of 1995.
TAMPA, Florida - The Freight Connection says its board of directors named Rock Gaetz to serve as president and chief executive.
NEW YORK - Kiwi International Airlines says it would suspend flight after failing to get a U.S. Bankruptcy Court to approve the proposed financing it needed to continue operating.
RIO DE JANEIRO - Senior company officials say Varig is spending around $31 million dollars over the next two years to revamp its corporate image in an effort to return to profitability.
**OCTOBER 16**
MIAMI - An Aeroflot executive says demand for imported flowers is so great in Russia that Aeroflot is mulling adding a freighter through Miami international airport.
HONG KONG - Cathay Pacific says it has retired the last of its Lockheed TriStars.
AMSTERDAM - Air airport statement says Eindhoven airport has seen as 11 percent increase in cargo volumes in the first nine months of the year.
BRUSSELS - Virgin Express CEO Jonathan Ornstein says "we will make an offer for Air Liberte".
LJUBLJANA - Slovenia's Adria Airways says it carried 473,000 passengers in the first nine months of 1996, up 11 percent on the same period of 1995.
DUBLIN - Aer Rianta says passenger traffic at Dublin airport in the first nine months of 1996 was 14 percent ahead of the same period the previous year.

STRASBOURG - Airport authority figures show air cargo traffic handled at Strasbourg-Entzeim airport in the first nine months of the year totalled 5,101 tonnes, up 10.3 percent on the same period in 1995.
PARIS - France's civil aviation authority, the DGAC, says it had maintained some all-cargo flights in a minimum service flight programme for the first time.
PARIS - Le Monde says Air France was expected to announce a strategic agreement with U.S. airlines Delta and Continental.
COPENHAGEN - Denmark's national statistics office says Danish shipping companies' combined earnings rose to 5.7 billion crowns in 1995, a 21 percent rise from 1994's 4.7 billion.
LONDON - BA says it was increasing full published fares on its European routes by an average 2.5 percent from the middle of October.
* BA says the rise in Europe was a direct consequence of the soaring cost of jet-fuel, which has risen by 30 percent since the middle of July, and it was considering increases on long-haul routes.

PARIS - Le Monde, reporting a planned tie-up between Air France and both Continental and Delta airlines says the deals would involve so-called code-sharing, and a variety of joint marketing and sales programme.
HONG KONG - The chief executive of BA Robert Ayling defended the airline's proposed alliance with American Airlines which has been criticised by rival airlines as an effort to block competition.
PARIS - Air France Cargo says it had placed an embargo on perishable shipments, live animals and urgent freight as a result of a "work to rule" by airline staff at its Charles de Gualle hub.
LONDON - The chief executive of Britain's Post Office says that he was worried that the bid by its Dutch equivalent for TNT would give it a stepping stone into the British postal market.
FRANKFURT - Lufthansa Cargo says its new Internet home page will be primarily an information service for the air cargo industry.
FRANKFURT - The country's airports association says Germany should impose strict conditions on de-regulation if airport ground handling services.
HONG KONG - American cargo carrier Evergreen International airlines says it has increased the number of flights from Hong Kong due of high trans-Pacific demand.
MADRID - Airlines and general sales agents say demand for air cargo space ex-Madrid had soared this month, particularly on routes to Latin America and the Far East as the peak export season starts.
AMSTERDAM - KLM says it would decide shortly whether to hike tariffs to offset spiralling fuel prices.
STOCKHOLM - Sweden's civil aviation administration Luftfartsverket says Swedish airports handled 14 percent more cargo in September this year than the same period last year.
HONG KONG - BA chief executive Robert Ayling says it plans to offer more passenger flights to Hong Kong but will not be changing the current wet lease freighter service to the territory.
* BA's Ayling says it plans to offer more flights between Hong Kong and London and wants to start a new service to Shanghai "as soon as possible".
PARIS - Air France, confirming commercial alliances with Delta and Continental, says the link-ups would widen each partner's market access and improve services for both passengers and freight.
ZURICH - Swissair says it saw no danger to its trans-Atlantic alliance with Delta from a new co-operation pack between Delta, Air France and Continental.
HELSINKI - A Finnair spokesman says it does not plan to increase its fares despite sharply higher jet fuel prices.
ORLANDO - Enterprise Florida says international trade through Florida's totalled $26.9 billion in the first half of 1996, an increase of 3.5 percent or $900 million over the same period last year.

PARIS - The comite Interprofessionel du Fret says the air cargo community at Paris' Charles de Gualle airport has activated an emergency sub-committee to keep the industry informed of the impact of labour disputes.
